key_insight: Prospective ICU AI deployment reveals that the biggest uncertainty is not model accuracy alone, but how the system fits workflow, governance, and learning processes in real clinical operations.
clinical_relevance: Early-stage clinical AI pilots should be designed to test operational use, accountability, and data-governance requirements alongside performance to support safer, more informed deployment decisions.
method: Prospective, single-center mixed-methods implementation study in a surgical ICU
Evaluated 267 consecutive ICU stays with an AI-based length-of-stay decision support system
Assessed workflow fit, governance/data protection, live benchmarking, ethics/accountability, and human-AI interaction
evidence_signal: In routine use, the low-burden "glance-and-judge" workflow was adopted by consultants (72%) and residents (61%), while governance constraints required an air-gapped setup with once-daily data refreshes and some stale case-list entries (2.7%).
watch_item: Operational and governance safeguards improved compliance but introduced latency and occasional outdated information, which may limit real-time usefulness in fast-changing ICU settings.
paper_title: Managing AI-Enabled Uncertainty in Clinical AI Deployment: Mixed-Methods Study of Governance, Workflow, and Organizational Learning in an ICU Decision Support Pilot
